:::{#def-pairwise-disjoint}
#### Pairwise disjoint sets

Finitely or countably many sets $A_1, A_2, \ldots$
are **pairwise disjoint**
(also called **disjoint** or **mutually disjoint**)
when no two of them share an element:

$$A_i \cap A_j = \emptyset \quad \text{for all } i \neq j$$

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#rem-mutually-exclusive}
#### Mutually exclusive events

In probability, pairwise disjoint events are usually called **mutually exclusive**.
For example, for one roll of a six-sided die,
the events "the roll is even", $\set{2, 4, 6}$,
and "the roll is odd", $\set{1, 3, 5}$,
are mutually exclusive:
no roll is both even and odd.

:::
